2251.title: Sexual exploitation of children

rows.trigger: Production offense. Employing, using, persuading, inducing, enticing, or coercing a minor to engage in, or having a minor assist another to engage in, or transporting a minor in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or in any Territory or Possession with intent that the minor engage in, sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing a visual depiction or transmitting a live visual depiction, on any of three interstate hooks (knowledge or reason to know the depiction will be transported or transmitted or mailed; production or transmission using materials that traveled in commerce; or actual transport or transmission or mailing). No dollar amount, no quantity, and no count of any kind is an element, so min and max are null. scope is null: nothing in this paragraph narrows it beyond value by a countable dwelling, item, prior, victim, or place. The phrase 'any minor' states the class of person the conduct must involve, which is the offense definition itself, not a narrowing of who the victim is within a broader offense, so 'victim' does not apply. No 'except as provided in' clause appears anywhere in section 2251. Punishment comes entirely by cross-reference: 'shall be punished as provided under subsection (e)', which supplies fine plus 15 to 30 years, 25 to 50 years on one qualifying prior, and 35 years to life on 2 or more qualifying priors.
rows.quote: Any person who employs, uses, persuades, induces, entices, or coerces any minor to engage in, or who has a minor assist any other person to engage in, or who transports any minor in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce, or in any Territory or Possession of the United States, with the intent that such minor engage in, any sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing any visual depiction of such conduct or for the purpose of transmitting a live visual depiction of such conduct, shall be punished as provided under subsection (e), if such person knows or has reason to know that such visual depiction will be transported or transmitted using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed, if that visual depiction was produced or transmitted using materials that have been mailed, shipped, or transported in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means, including by computer, or if such visual depiction has actually been transported or transmitted using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed.

rows.trigger: Parent, legal guardian, or person having custody or control of a minor who knowingly permits the minor to engage in, or to assist another to engage in, sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing a visual depiction or transmitting a live visual depiction, on the same three interstate hooks as (a). No dollar amount, quantity, or count is an element, so min and max are null. scope is null: the custodial relationship describes who the DEFENDANT must be, not who the victim is, and in any event it is the offense definition rather than a narrowing threshold, so 'victim' is wrong here. Punishment comes only by cross-reference: 'shall be punished as provided under subsection (e) of this section', supplying fine plus 15 to 30 years, 25 to 50 years on one qualifying prior, and 35 years to life on 2 or more qualifying priors.
rows.quote: Any parent, legal guardian, or person having custody or control of a minor who knowingly permits such minor to engage in, or to assist any other person to engage in, sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing any visual depiction of such conduct or for the purpose of transmitting a live visual depiction of such conduct shall be punished as provided under subsection (e) of this section, if such parent, legal guardian, or person knows or has reason to know that such visual depiction will be transported or transmitted using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed, if that visual depiction was produced or transmitted using materials that have been mailed, shipped, or transported in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means, including by computer, or if such visual depiction has actually been transported or transmitted using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed.

rows.trigger: Extraterritorial production. The same employing, using, persuading, inducing, enticing, or coercing conduct as (a), committed outside of the United States, its territories or possessions, for the purpose of producing a visual depiction, and only 'in a circumstance described in paragraph (2)'. No dollar amount, quantity, or count is an element, so min and max are null. scope is null 'outside of the United States' is where the conduct occurs as part of the offense definition, and it is not a countable narrowing of a value threshold, which is what the scope field records. Punishment comes only by cross-reference: 'shall be punished as provided under subsection (e)', supplying fine plus 15 to 30 years, 25 to 50 years on one qualifying prior, and 35 years to life on 2 or more qualifying priors.
rows.quote: Any person who, in a circumstance described in paragraph (2), employs, uses, persuades, induces, entices, or coerces any minor to engage in, or who has a minor assist any other person to engage in, any sexually explicit conduct outside of the United States, its territories or possessions, for the purpose of producing any visual depiction of such conduct, shall be punished as provided under subsection (e).

rows.trigger: Jurisdictional circumstance element for (c)(1). It creates no offense of its own, cross-references no penalty subsection, and states no value, quantity, or count, so min, max, and scope are all null. Both subparagraphs read in full and either alternative suffices: (A) the person intends the visual depiction to be transported to the United States, its territories or possessions, or (B) the person actually transports it there. Neither states a lower or upper bound of any kind.
rows.quote: The circumstance referred to in paragraph (1) is that- (A) the person intends such visual depiction to be transported to the United States, its territories or possessions, by any means, including by using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or mail; or (B) the person transports such visual depiction to the United States, its territories or possessions, by any means, including by using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or mail.

rows.trigger: Advertising offense. Knowingly making, printing, or publishing, or causing to be made, printed, or published, any notice or advertisement seeking or offering either (A) to receive, exchange, buy, produce, display, distribute, or reproduce any visual depiction whose production involves a minor engaging in sexually explicit conduct, or (B) participation in any act of sexually explicit conduct by or with a minor for the purpose of producing a visual depiction, and only 'in a circumstance described in paragraph (2)'. Both subparagraphs were read; the penalty sits in a flush passage after them ('shall be punished as provided under subsection (e)') and reaches both alternatives. scope is null read literally, 'item' asserts a threshold counted in items, and this paragraph states no count of notices, advertisements, or depictions. The object is simply 'any notice or advertisement', and a single one suffices, so there is no item quantity to scope to. No dollar amount either, so min and max are null. Punishment comes only by cross-reference to subsection (e): fine plus 15 to 30 years, 25 to 50 years on one qualifying prior, and 35 years to life on 2 or more qualifying priors.
rows.quote: Any person who, in a circumstance described in paragraph (2), knowingly makes, prints, or publishes, or causes to be made, printed, or published, any notice or advertisement seeking or offering- (A) to receive, exchange, buy, produce, display, distribute, or reproduce, any visual depiction, if the production of such visual depiction involves the use of a minor engaging in sexually explicit conduct and such visual depiction is of such conduct; or (B) participation in any act of sexually explicit conduct by or with any minor for the purpose of producing a visual depiction of such conduct; shall be punished as provided under subsection (e).

rows.trigger: Jurisdictional circumstance element for (d)(1). It creates no offense of its own, cross-references no penalty subsection, and states no value, quantity, or count, so min, max, and scope are all null. Both subparagraphs read in full and either alternative suffices: (A) the person knows or has reason to know the notice or advertisement will be transported in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed, or (B) the notice or advertisement is actually so transported or mailed.
rows.quote: The circumstance referred to in paragraph (1) is that- (A) such person knows or has reason to know that such notice or advertisement will be transported using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means including by computer or mailed; or (B) such notice or advertisement is transported using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means including by computer or mailed.

rows.trigger: Base penalty tier for an INDIVIDUAL, first offense (no qualifying prior conviction). Cross-reference mapping: subsection (e) reaches back by the words 'violates ... this section', so this tier punishes every conduct provision in the section, namely (a), (b), (c)(1), and (d)(1); (c)(2) and (d)(2) are circumstance elements and are not separately punished. Penalty: fined under this title AND imprisoned not less than 15 years nor more than 30 years. The 15 years is a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment and the 30 years is the statutory maximum term; a term of imprisonment is never a min/max trigger, and 'fined under this title' is a penalty, never a trigger. No dollar, quantity, or count element exists, so min and max are null. scope is null: this tier is by its own terms the NON-recidivist tier, so 'prior' would state the exact opposite of the truth.
rows.quote: Any individual who violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section shall be fined under this title and imprisoned not less than 15 years nor more than 30 years...

rows.trigger: Attempt and conspiracy. The words 'or attempts or conspires to violate' sit inside the same sentence that sets the individual penalty, so an attempt or a conspiracy to violate (a), (b), (c)(1), or (d)(1) carries the identical range: fine plus 15 to 30 years, escalating to 25 to 50 years on one qualifying prior and 35 years to life on 2 or more qualifying priors. The organization sentence contains the same 'attempts or conspires' language, so an organization's attempt or conspiracy likewise draws a fine under this title. No reduced or separate range is stated for inchoate conduct anywhere in the section. No dollar, quantity, or count element, so min and max are null; scope is null because no countable narrowing applies, and this row is not conditioned on a criminal history.
rows.quote: Any individual who violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section shall be fined under this title and imprisoned not less than 15 years nor more than 30 years... Any organization that violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section shall be fined under this title.

rows.trigger: Recidivist tier, ONE prior conviction. Applies to an individual who violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, (a), (b), (c)(1), or (d)(1). Penalty: fined under this title and imprisoned not less than 25 years nor more than 50 years. Qualifying priors under this tier: this chapter (chapter 110), section 1591, chapter 71, chapter 109A, or chapter 117; the Uniform Code of Military Justice; or the laws of any State relating to aggravated sexual abuse, sexual abuse, abusive sexual contact involving a minor or ward, or sex trafficking of children, or the production, possession, receipt, mailing, sale, distribution, shipment, or transportation of child pornography. Note the asymmetry, verified against the fetched text: section 1591 and the itemized child-pornography-conduct clause appear in THIS one-prior list only and NOT in the 2-or-more list. Terms of years are not value thresholds and the fine is a penalty cap, so min and max are null.
rows.quote: ...but if such person has one prior conviction under this chapter, section 1591, chapter 71, chapter 109A, or chapter 117, or under the Uniform Code of Military Justice or the laws of any State relating to aggravated sexual abuse, sexual abuse, abusive sexual contact involving a minor or ward, or sex trafficking of children, or the production, possession, receipt, mailing, sale, distribution, shipment, or transportation of child pornography, such person shall be fined under this title and imprisoned for not less than 25 years nor more than 50 years...

rows.trigger: Recidivist tier, 2 OR MORE prior convictions. Applies to an individual who violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, (a), (b), (c)(1), or (d)(1). Penalty: fined under this title and imprisoned not less than 35 years nor more than life. Qualifying priors under this tier are a NARROWER list than the one-prior tier: this chapter (chapter 110), chapter 71, chapter 109A, or chapter 117; the Uniform Code of Military Justice; or the laws of any State relating to the sexual exploitation of children. Section 1591 does not appear here, and the itemized child-pornography-conduct clause is replaced by the single phrase 'relating to the sexual exploitation of children'. 'Life' is the ceiling of the sentence, not a value threshold, so min and max are null.
rows.quote: ...but if such person has 2 or more prior convictions under this chapter, chapter 71, chapter 109A, or chapter 117, or under the Uniform Code of Military Justice or the laws of any State relating to the sexual exploitation of children, such person shall be fined under this title and imprisoned not less than 35 years nor more than life.

rows.trigger: Organizational defendant. A separate sentence of subsection (e) punishing an organization that violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section, meaning (a), (b), (c)(1), or (d)(1). Penalty is a fine under this title only. No term of imprisonment is stated for an organization, and none of the three individual tiers, including the two recidivist tiers, applies to it by its terms ('Any individual ... such person'). A fine is a penalty, never a trigger, so min and max are null; scope is null because no countable narrowing and no criminal-history condition applies.
rows.quote: Any organization that violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section shall be fined under this title.

rows.trigger: Death-results enhancement, the final sentence of subsection (e). Applies to 'Whoever, in the course of an offense under this section, engages in conduct that results in the death of a person', so it reaches any offense under (a), (b), (c)(1), or (d)(1) and, unlike the three graduated tiers, is not limited to individuals and is not conditioned on any prior conviction. Penalty: death, or imprisonment for not less than 30 years, or for life. The 30 years is a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment, not a value threshold, so min and max are null. scope is null 'conduct that results in the death of a person' is a result element, not a threshold counted in victims, and 'a person' is not limited to the minor, so nothing here narrows the row by who the victim is.
rows.quote: Whoever, in the course of an offense under this section, engages in conduct that results in the death of a person, shall be punished by death or imprisoned for not less than 30 years or for life.

1030.title: 18 U.S.C. 1030, fraud and related activity in connection with computers: verified penalty table

rows.trigger: CHAPEAU AND FLUSH CLOSER of the offense subsection. The chapeau 'Whoever-' opens paragraphs (1) through (7); the flush sentence after (a)(7)(C) converts every one of them into a subsection (c) penalty. No dollar element, no quantity element, no term of years of its own, so min and max are null.
rows.quote: (a) Whoever- ... shall be punished as provided in subsection (c) of this section.

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW, not a penalty tier. National defense / foreign relations information or restricted data. PUNISHED BY: (c)(1)(A), imprisonment not more than ten years where the offense does not occur after a conviction for another offense under this section; and (c)(1)(B), imprisonment not more than twenty years where it does occur after such a conviction. Conspiracy and attempt reach it through (b), which routes back to the same (c)(1) tiers. NO LOWER BOUND: the paragraph states no dollar amount and no quantity, so min and max are null. Restricted data is defined by cross-reference to paragraph y. of section 11 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2014(y)).
rows.quote: (1) having knowingly accessed a computer without authorization or exceeding authorized access, and by means of such conduct having obtained information that has been determined by the United States Government pursuant to an Executive order or statute to require protection against unauthorized disclosure for reasons of national defense or foreign relations, or any restricted data, as defined in paragraph y. of section 11 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, with reason to believe that such information so obtained could be used to the injury of the United States, or to the advantage of any foreign nation willfully communicates, delivers, transmits, or causes to be communicated, delivered, or transmitted, or attempts to communicate, deliver, transmit or cause to be communicated, delivered, or transmitted the same to any person not entitled to receive it, or willfully retains the same and fails to deliver it to the officer or employee of the United States entitled to receive it;

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW, chapeau of the unauthorized-obtaining paragraph. Intentional access without authorization, or exceeding authorized access, thereby obtaining any of the three categories in subparagraphs (A), (B), (C). PUNISHED BY: (c)(2)(A), one year, first offense, unless (c)(2)(B) applies; (c)(2)(B), 5 years, for (a)(2) ALONE, where any of clauses (i), (ii) or (iii) is met; (c)(2)(C), ten years, where the offense occurs after a conviction for another offense under this section. NO LOWER BOUND: the paragraph states no dollar amount and no quantity.
rows.quote: (2) intentionally accesses a computer without authorization or exceeds authorized access, and thereby obtains-

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW. Financial-record branch of (a)(2). No dollar amount and no quantity is stated, so min and max are null. 'Financial institution' is defined at (e)(4) and 'financial record' at (e)(5). The printed text carries footnote 1 after 'section 1602(n)' pointing to the References in Text note that section 1602(n) of title 15 was redesignated section 1602(o) by Pub. L. 111-203.
rows.quote: (A) information contained in a financial record of a financial institution, or of a card issuer as defined in section 1602(n) of title 15, or contained in a file of a consumer reporting agency on a consumer, as such terms are defined in the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.);

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW. United States department or agency branch of (a)(2). No dollar amount and no quantity, so min and max are null. 'Department of the United States' is defined at (e)(7).
rows.quote: (B) information from any department or agency of the United States; or

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW. Protected-computer branch of (a)(2), and the widest of the three: it reaches ordinary private-sector data, because 'protected computer' at (e)(2)(B) covers any computer used in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or communication. The 2008 amendment (Pub. L. 110-326, sec. 203) struck the former requirement that 'the conduct involved an interstate or foreign communication'. No dollar amount and no quantity, so min and max are null.
rows.quote: (C) information from any protected computer;

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW. Intentional access to a nonpublic United States department or agency computer without authorization to access it. PUNISHED BY: (c)(2)(A), one year, first offense; and (c)(2)(C), ten years, where the offense occurs after a conviction for another offense under this section. NOT reachable by (c)(2)(B), which names only (a)(2). NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar amount and no quantity is stated.
rows.quote: (3) intentionally, without authorization to access any nonpublic computer of a department or agency of the United States, accesses such a computer of that department or agency that is exclusively for the use of the Government of the United States or, in the case of a computer not exclusively for such use, is used by or for the Government of the United States and such conduct affects that use by or for the Government of the United States;

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW, not a penalty tier. PUNISHED BY: (c)(3)(A), imprisonment not more than five years where the offense does not occur after a conviction for another offense under this section; and (c)(3)(B), imprisonment not more than ten years where it does. NO LOWER BOUND. The offense reaches obtaining 'anything of value' with no dollar floor at all. The $5,000 figure is a CARVE-OUT, not a trigger threshold: it removes from the offense only the case where the object of the fraud AND the thing obtained consist ONLY of the use of the computer and that use is worth not more than $5,000 in any 1-year period. If anything other than mere computer use is obtained, no dollar amount is required. min is therefore null, and scope is null because the paragraph contains no count of items and nothing else that narrows a value threshold.
rows.quote: (4) knowingly and with intent to defraud, accesses a protected computer without authorization, or exceeds authorized access, and by means of such conduct furthers the intended fraud and obtains anything of value, unless the object of the fraud and the thing obtained consists only of the use of the computer and the value of such use is not more than $5,000 in any 1-year period;

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW. Knowing transmission of a program, information, code or command that intentionally causes damage without authorization to a protected computer. PUNISHED BY: (c)(4)(B)(i), not more than 10 years, first offense, if the offense caused or would have caused a harm in subclauses (I) through (VI) of (c)(4)(A)(i), except as provided in (E) and (F); (c)(4)(C)(i), not more than 20 years, where it occurs after a conviction for another offense under this section, except as provided in (E) and (F); (c)(4)(E), not more than 20 years, for serious bodily injury; (c)(4)(F), any term of years or life, for death; and, if none of those conditions is met, (c)(4)(G)(i), not more than 1 year. NO LOWER BOUND: 'damage' at (e)(8) states no amount.
rows.quote: (5)(A) knowingly causes the transmission of a program, information, code, or command, and as a result of such conduct, intentionally causes damage without authorization, to a protected computer;

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW. Intentional access to a protected computer without authorization that recklessly causes damage. PUNISHED BY: (c)(4)(A)(i), not more than 5 years, first offense, if the offense caused or would have caused a harm in subclauses (I) through (VI), except as provided in (E) and (F); (c)(4)(C)(i), not more than 20 years, where it occurs after a conviction for another offense under this section; and otherwise (c)(4)(G)(i), not more than 1 year. NOTE the mapping trap: (c)(4)(E) and (c)(4)(F) reach only conduct 'in violation of subsection (a)(5)(A)', so the serious-bodily-injury and death enhancements do NOT attach to (a)(5)(B). NO LOWER BOUND.
rows.quote: (B) intentionally accesses a protected computer without authorization, and as a result of such conduct, recklessly causes damage; or

rows.trigger: ELEMENT ROW, and the sharpest cross-reference in the section. Intentional access to a protected computer without authorization causing damage AND loss. PUNISHED BY: (c)(4)(D)(i), not more than 10 years, ONLY where the offense occurs after a conviction for another offense under this section. A bare first offense under (a)(5)(C) fits none of (c)(4)(A) through (F), because (A) names only (a)(5)(B), (B) names only (a)(5)(A), (C) names only (a)(5)(A) and (B), and (E) and (F) name only (a)(5)(A); it therefore falls to the catch-all at (c)(4)(G)(i), not more than 1 year. NO LOWER BOUND: neither 'damage' (e)(8) nor 'loss' (e)(11) carries any stated amount. The printed text carries footnote 2, 'So in original. The period probably should be a semicolon.'
rows.quote: (C) intentionally accesses a protected computer without authorization, and as a result of such conduct, causes damage and loss.

There is no subsection after (e) and no carve-out clause. Every one of these appears in the table, and every provision that assigns a punishment, a mandatory minimum, or an enhancement has a row. Nothing is missing.
unread: The table's unread block is substantively adequate: it correctly identifies the Source Credit, Codification, Amendments, Short Title, Severability, and Findings notes as read-but-not-rowed editorial matter, and correctly identifies the contents of the cross-referenced bodies (18 U.S.C. 1591, chapters 71, 109A, 117, 110, and the UCMJ) as outside the section. I independently confirmed the 2006 amendment note: it inserted 'section 1591' after 'one prior conviction under this chapter', i.e. into the one-prior list only, which is exactly why the two lists differ. The only complaint is the process-narration framing of unread[0], recorded above.
2251.notes:
PENALTY DATA IS RIGHT. Walking the checks in order.

1. Missing penalty provisions: none. All four conduct paragraphs, both circumstance paragraphs, and all four sentences of (e) are present.

2. Cross-references, walked one by one. Subsection (e) reaches back by the words "violates ... this section", so it punishes (a), (b), (c)(1), and (d)(1), and (c)(2)/(d)(2) are circumstance elements that are separately punished by nothing. Every (e) row maps to exactly that set and no other. Three finer mappings are also right and are the ones easiest to get wrong: (i) the two recidivist tiers are limited to individuals, because the sentence opens "Any individual" and the recidivist clauses continue with "such person", so they do not reach the organization row; (ii) the death-results sentence opens "Whoever" and is therefore NOT limited to individuals and NOT conditioned on any prior, which the table states explicitly; (iii) the (d)(1) penalty sits in a flush passage after subparagraphs (A) and (B) and reaches both, which the table captures. No mis-mapping found.

3. Terms, minimums, fines. Base 15 to 30 years plus fine; one prior 25 to 50 years plus fine; 2 or more priors 35 years to life plus fine; organization fine under this title with no imprisonment; death results, death or not less than 30 years or life. All five match the fetched text exactly. No fine is converted to a dollar figure anywhere, which is correct for "fined under this title".

4. The two qualifying-prior lists, the item this round was told to verify. Both are right, including the asymmetry. One-prior list: this chapter, section 1591, chapter 71, chapter 109A, chapter 117, the UCMJ, or state laws relating to aggravated sexual abuse, sexual abuse, abusive sexual contact involving a minor or ward, or sex trafficking of children, or the production, possession, receipt, mailing, sale, distribution, shipment, or transportation of child pornography. Two-or-more list: this chapter, chapter 71, chapter 109A, chapter 117, the UCMJ, or state laws relating to the sexual exploitation of children. Section 1591 is absent from the second list and the itemized child-pornography clause collapses to the single phrase "relating to the sexual exploitation of children". The table states the narrowing on the correct tier and pairs each list with the correct term (25/50 and 35/life). The 2006 amendment note independently corroborates the asymmetry.

5. Invented bounds and thresholds: none. Section 2251 contains no dollar value and no quantity element, and every min and max in the table is null. Critically, no term of years has been typed into min or max, which is the failure mode this schema invites. No strict threshold appears in the statute ("not less than" is inclusive), so there is nothing that should have carried minExclusive.

6. level: null on all twelve rows. Correct for a federal statute.

7. scope: "prior" appears on exactly the two recidivist tiers and nowhere else. The base tier is correctly left null rather than marked "prior", which would invert its meaning. Recording the count of priors in trigger text with null bounds is the settled convention and I am not treating it as a defect.

8. Quotes: I mechanically checked all twelve, not just five, by normalizing whitespace and testing each segment as a literal substring of the fetched text. Every segment matches verbatim. Every elision is marked with an ellipsis, including the two-sentence splice in the attempt/conspiracy row. The (c)(2), (d)(2), and (d)(1) quotes join subparagraphs across source line breaks with a space, which drops no words.

The only defects I found are the residual argument and process text listed in "wrong". Under the materiality rule they are notes, not failures: none of them changes a term, a minimum, a fine, a mapping, or a bound, and a page built from this table would state the law correctly. But they are real, they are the same class of defect the last round was patched for, and the patch was scoped only to the two (e) recidivist rows while the same text sat in four other triggers. If another pass is spent on this table, that is the one thing to strip, and it is a find-and-delete job, not a re-derivation.

Two granularity observations offered as notes only, per convention 3. First, four rows share the bare cite "18 U.S.C. 2251(e)": the base tier, the attempt/conspiracy row, the organization row, and the death-results row. Their penalties differ (15-30 years, fine only, death/30-life), so a downstream consumer keying on cite alone gets a four-way collision. Convention 2's parenthetical disambiguation is already in the table for the recidivist pair and would extend cleanly here, as "(e) (organization)" and "(e) (death results)". I am not failing the table for this because each row's own penalty content is correct and unambiguous within the row, and convention 2 as written addresses the two tiers that were already fixed. Second, the attempt/conspiracy row duplicates the base tier's cite and range and adds no penalty content the base row lacks; folding it in would lose nothing, but keeping it is the builder's call.

On the conventions themselves, invited by the instruction: I have no objection to any of the four. Keeping a count of priors out of min/max is right, since a lookup on quantity should not return a row about a record.

1030.completeness: complete: every provision of 18 U.S.C. 1030 that assigns a punishment or an enhancement has a row — (c)(1)(A), (c)(1)(B), (c)(2)(A), (c)(2)(B) chapeau + clauses (i)/(ii)/(iii), (c)(2)(C), (c)(3)(A), (c)(3)(B), (c)(4)(A)(i) + subclauses (I)-(VI), (c)(4)(A)(ii), (c)(4)(B)(i)/(ii), (c)(4)(C)(i)/(ii), (c)(4)(D)(i)/(ii), (c)(4)(E), (c)(4)(F), (c)(4)(G)(i)/(ii) — plus the (b) inchoate route and the (i)/(j) mandatory forfeiture. Every (c)(4) subparagraph chapeau is quoted verbatim inside its (i) row, so no penalty text is unquoted anywhere. All 55 rows carry element or definitional context; nothing in the operative text is absent.
1030.notes:
VERDICT BASIS. I found no defect a page could repeat and be wrong. Detail by check:

1. MISSING PENALTY PROVISIONS: none. See completeness field.

2. CROSS-REFERENCES (the load-bearing check). Walked all of them, penalty-to-conduct and conduct-to-penalty, and every one is right. (c)(1)(A)/(B) -> (a)(1) only. (c)(2)(A) -> (a)(2),(a)(3),(a)(6). (c)(2)(B) -> (a)(2) ALONE, and the (a)(3) and (a)(6) rows both say so explicitly. (c)(2)(C) -> (a)(2),(a)(3),(a)(6). (c)(3)(A)/(B) -> (a)(4),(a)(7). (c)(4)(A)(i) -> (a)(5)(B) only. (c)(4)(B)(i) -> (a)(5)(A) only, incorporating harms (I)-(VI) of (A)(i). (c)(4)(C)(i) -> (a)(5)(A) or (B), recidivist, and correctly does NOT reach (a)(5)(C). (c)(4)(D)(i) -> (a)(5)(C), recidivist only. (c)(4)(E)/(F) -> conduct "in violation of subsection (a)(5)(A)" ONLY; the table flags this trap in the (a)(5)(B) row and does not attach the injury/death enhancements to (a)(5)(B) or (a)(5)(C). (c)(4)(G) catch-all correctly carries a bare (a)(5)(C) first offense and any (a)(5) offense with no qualifying harm. The three paragraphs the page rests on are exact: (a)(1) -> 10/20; (a)(4) -> 5/10; (a)(5) -> 5 (B first), 10 (A first), 20 (A or B repeat), 10 (C repeat), 20 SBI, any term or life for death, 1 year catch-all.

3. TERMS, MINIMUMS, FINES: all fourteen terms verified word for word against the source (ten, twenty, one, 5, ten, five, ten, 5, 10, 20, 10, 20, any term of years or life, 1). The section contains no mandatory minimum and the table invents none. Fines are uniformly recorded as "a fine under this title," never as a threshold.

4. BOUNDS AND THRESHOLDS: no invented floor or ceiling anywhere. Every max is null, correct since no (c) tier states a conduct ceiling. The (a)(4) $5,000 is correctly recorded as null with the carve-out reasoning in trigger, not typed as a threshold. (e)(10)'s "more than 1 year," (g)'s 2-year limitations period and (h)'s 3-year reporting duration are all correctly null. The PATCH VERIFIES: (c)(2)(B)(iii) reads "the value of the information obtained exceeds $5,000" and the row now carries min 5000 with minExclusive true. The two inclusive figures are correctly left inclusive by contrast: (c)(4)(A)(i)(I) "aggregating at least $5,000" (min 5000, no minExclusive) and (c)(4)(A)(i)(VI) "10 or more protected computers" (min 10). No strict threshold is recorded as inclusive.

5. LEVEL: null on all 55 rows.

6. SCOPE: "prior" appears on exactly the five recidivist tiers, (c)(1)(B), (c)(2)(C), (c)(3)(B), (c)(4)(C)(i), (c)(4)(D)(i), and nowhere else; each has min and max null with the prior-conviction condition described in trigger, per the settled convention. "item" appears once, on (c)(4)(A)(i)(VI), where the threshold is literally a count of protected computers. No misuse.

7. QUOTES: I checked all 55 programmatically, not five. Every quote is verbatim contiguous source text; every elision is marked with "..." ((a), (c)(2)(B) chapeau); no splice or paraphrase. The only three deltas are OLRC footnote-reference digits dropped from mid-sentence ("section 1602(n) 1", "(a)(4),4", "subclauses 5"), and each of those three rows names the footnote and its content in trigger. Historical assertions spot-checked and confirmed against the Amendments notes: (c)(5) struck by Pub. L. 110-326 sec. 204(a)(2)(D); (a)(2)(C) interstate-communication clause struck by sec. 203; (h) enactment date Sept. 13, 1994; footnote texts 2 through 6 verbatim.

8. ARGUMENT IN FIELDS: no process argument, no answer to an auditor, no defense of a convention. Nothing resembling the rebuttal-in-a-data-field problem from the prior round. What is present is a milder habit: a handful of triggers justify their own field values rather than only describing the provision. "RECIDIVIST TIER, correctly scope 'prior'" on five rows; "the one row in this table where scope 'item' is literally correct" at (c)(4)(A)(i)(VI), which is table-referential rather than statute-referential; "scope is null, NOT 'victim' ... a per-victim reading would be wrong on the face of the word 'aggregating'" at (c)(4)(A)(i)(I); "CRITICAL TO THE NO-FLOOR READING" at (e)(8). Each is legally accurate and none can make a downstream penalty wrong, so under the materiality rule these are notes. Recommend a copy pass that drops the word "correctly," the phrase "the one row in this table," and the pre-emptive "NOT 'victim'" framing, keeping the substantive statutory reasoning that follows.

THE (d) QUESTION, decided: NOTE, not a defect. (d) is investigative authority and assigns no punishment, no minimum and no enhancement, so nothing a penalty page renders can be wrong because (d)(2) and (d)(3) are paraphrased in trigger rather than quoted. The quote field is honest about what it quotes and the paraphrase of (d)(2) and (d)(3) is accurate against the source. If the builder wants the cite and the quote to line up exactly, the cleaner fix is to relabel the cite "(d)(1)" and add short (d)(2) and (d)(3) rows, or to extend the quote to all three paragraphs. Either is cosmetic.

OTHER NOTES, none failing. (a) The (b) row lists twelve tiers that "additionally punish attempts in their own terms" but omits (c)(4)(C)(i) and (c)(4)(D)(i), each of which reads "an offense or an attempt to commit an offense"; the (ii) clauses of those same subparagraphs are listed, so no attempt route is actually unrepresented. (b) The (a)(5)(B) row repeats the "except as provided in subparagraphs (E) and (F)" language from the (c)(4)(A) chapeau before explaining that (E) and (F) cannot reach (a)(5)(B); both statements are correct, but a reader could take the first clause as a live carve-out for (a)(5)(B) conduct. Consider leading with the limitation. (c) Granularity is sound as built: the (c)(4) subparagraph chapeaux folded into their (i) rows all carry their penalty text verbatim, so a lookup on any of them returns the term.

ON THE CONVENTIONS THEMSELVES: I have no objection. Keeping a count of priors out of min and in trigger with scope "prior" is right for a lookup table keyed on conduct thresholds, and this section is a good demonstration of why, since its recidivist tiers turn on nothing but criminal history and would otherwise pollute five rows with a bare "1".
